title: Corner C4 - Welcome to Your Corner Reveal Spec
summary: The hero reveal moment when a new client first sees their Corner office. Beat-by-beat choreography. This is the moment that makes people say 'holy shit.' Bobby builds this from frame-perfect specs.
content:
Corner C4: "Welcome to Your Corner" Reveal Spec

Steffen | 2026-03-16 For Bobby. This is the single most important animation in the product. The moment a client goes from "I'm signing up for software" to "I have a team." Every frame matters.

Context

The client has:

  1. Answered 6 onboarding questions (5 minutes)
  2. Described their dream office (30 seconds)
  3. Watched their rooms generate on a loading screen (60-90 seconds)

The loading screen is dark navy (#0A0F1E). The floor plan outline is complete. All rooms are filled. The loading text has faded out.

The client is staring at a dark screen with a subtle floor plan outline. They've been waiting. Building anticipation. Now we deliver.

The Reveal: 7 Beats, 8.5 Seconds

Beat 0: The Breath (0s - 0.8s)

What happens: Nothing visible. Intentional silence.

Why: Every great reveal has a beat of stillness before the drop. The loading text just faded out. The client expects something. We make them wait exactly 0.8 seconds. Not a full second (too long, feels broken). Not 0.5s (too fast, feels rushed). 0.8s is the sweet spot.

Technical: The floor plan outline dims from current opacity to 5% opacity over 400ms (ease-out), then holds at 5% for 400ms. The screen is almost completely dark.

Sound design note (future): This is where a low, barely audible rising tone would start. Not a sound we build now, but leave room for it.

Beat 1: The World Materializes (0.8s - 2.3s)

Duration: 1.5s

What happens: The simplified 2D floor plan outline transforms into the full isometric 3D Corner world.

Animation sequence:

  1. 0.8s-1.0s: Floor plan outline scales up from 0.7x to 1.0x (200ms, ease-out). The lines start as 2D (flat floor plan) and begin curving into isometric perspective.

  2. 1.0s-1.8s: The outline fills with depth. Walls rise from the floor (grow upward from 0 height to full height, 800ms, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)). Floors populate with texture (opacity 0 to 1, 600ms, ease-in-out). This should look like the office is being assembled by an invisible architect.

  3. 1.3s-2.3s: Lighting fades in. Room floors gain their warm wood/tile textures. Ambient glow from each room (per the room spec: Bobby's purple LED, Elon's green terminal glow, Steffen's golden sunlight). Lighting fade: 1000ms ease-in-out.

  4. Throughout (0.8s-2.3s): Particle effect. 40-60 tiny cream-colored particles (#FDF6EC at 30% opacity) drift upward from the floor plan. Each particle: 1-2px, random starting position within the floor plan bounds, drifts upward at 20-40px/s with slight horizontal drift (+/- 10px), fades from 30% to 0% opacity over its 2-3s lifetime. Particles feel like construction dust settling in reverse. They should be barely noticeable but add organic warmth.

Camera: Starts at overview zoom (0.7x, seeing the whole plan). Holds here through this beat. No camera movement yet.

Colors: Background stays dark navy (#0A0F1E). The office world is the only light source.

Beat 2: Rooms Snap In (2.3s - 4.0s)

Duration: 1.7s

What happens: Individual rooms populate with their furniture and personality, one by one.

Snap animation per room:

  1. Room content (furniture, wall decorations, equipment) appears with a snap: scale from 0.85 to 1.0, opacity 0 to 1, duration 180ms, easing: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) (spring overshoot to 1.03, settle to 1.0).
  2. On snap, a "thud" ripple: circular ring expanding from room center, 1px stroke in room's agent accent color at 15% opacity, expands from 0px to 24px radius, fades to 0%, duration 400ms.
  3. Room's ambient glow intensifies from 40% to 100% brightness over 200ms (coincides with the snap).

Stagger order (150ms between each room):

  1. Main Hall (center) -- the heart snaps in first
  2. Mom (adjacent to hall)
  3. Alex (adjacent to hall)
  4. Steffen (adjacent to hall)
  5. Colton (adjacent to hall)
  6. Cleo (adjacent to hall)
  7. Patrik (corner)
  8. Steve (corner)
  9. Bobby (outer)
  10. Jacob (outer)
  11. Tony (outer)
  12. Elmo (bottom)
  13. Elon (bottom)

This radiates outward from the center, which feels like the office coming alive from its heart.

Total time: 13 rooms x 150ms stagger = 1,950ms. First room at 2.3s, last room at ~4.25s. Trim to 120ms stagger if 150ms feels too slow (then 1,560ms total, last room at ~3.86s).

Camera: Begins a slow, barely perceptible zoom from 0.7x toward 1.0x during this beat. Not a dramatic zoom. Just a 300ms drift from 0.7x to 0.8x starting at 3.0s. Ease-in-out. The client should barely notice it pulling them closer.

Beat 3: Agents Appear (4.0s - 5.2s)

Duration: 1.2s

What happens: Agent sprites fade in at their desks, one by one. The office goes from furnished but empty to alive.

Agent appear animation:

  1. Sprite fades in: opacity 0 to 1, 250ms ease-in-out
  2. Simultaneously: a small "materialization" effect -- 3 tiny particles (agent accent color, 2px) burst outward from the agent's position and fade over 300ms
  3. Agent starts in idle state immediately (breathing animation begins)
  4. Status dot appears next to agent nameplate (green, pulsing)

Stagger: 80ms between agents. Same order as rooms (center-out). With 13 agents at 80ms = 1,040ms total.

Nameplates: Fade in 200ms after their agent. Space Grotesk 600, 11px, cream text. Per the C2 HUD spec.

Beat 4: Agent Greetings (5.2s - 7.2s)

Duration: 2.0s

What happens: 3-4 agents speak up with welcome messages. Speech bubbles appear with typewriter text.

Which agents greet (depends on the client's roster):

  • The "operations" agent (Mom equivalent) always greets first
  • 2-3 others from their specific roster
  • Maximum 4 greetings total (more feels chaotic)

Greeting content (template, agent name changes per client):

Agent Type Greeting
Operations "Morning, [FirstName]. I'll keep everything running smooth."
Email "I've got your inbox. Nothing falls through."
Calendar "Your schedule's in good hands."
Lead Response "Someone reaches out? I'm already on it."
Strategy "Ready to build something great, [FirstName]."
Builder "The tools are set up. Let's go."

Speech bubble animation:

  1. Bubble appears: fade in + scale from 0.8 to 1.0, 150ms ease-out (per c2-sprite-spec)
  2. Text types in: 25ms per character, cream text (#FDF6EC)
  3. Bubble holds for 3 seconds after text completes
  4. Bubble fades out: 200ms ease-in

Stagger between greetings: 400ms. First greeting at 5.2s, second at 5.6s, third at 6.0s, fourth at 6.4s. Bubbles overlap on screen (multiple visible at once). This creates a feeling of a team jumping to attention.

Camera: At 5.5s, camera begins zooming from 0.8x to 1.2x, centering on the Main Hall area. Duration: 1.5s. Easing: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1). The zoom pulls the client into the world. They're no longer observing from above; they're in the office.

Beat 5: "Welcome to Your Corner" Banner (6.5s - 8.0s)

Duration: 1.5s

What happens: The hero banner drops in. This is the title card.

Banner animation:

  1. Text entrance (6.5s): "Welcome to your Corner" slides down from 60px above its resting position, opacity 0 to 1, 450ms, easing: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) (spring, overshoots 3px, settles).
  2. Sub-text entrance (6.9s, 400ms after headline): "[Company Name]'s AI Command Center" fades in, opacity 0 to 1, 300ms ease-out. Positioned 16px below headline.
  3. Orange accent underline (7.1s): A thin line (2px height, 120px width) draws from center-outward under "Corner" in the headline. Color: --onb-accent. Duration: 400ms ease-out. Adds visual weight and AOM branding.

Banner typography:

  • Headline: Syne 800 (ExtraBold), 52px desktop / 36px tablet / 28px mobile
  • Color: #FDF6EC (cream)
  • "Corner" word: Slightly different treatment -- Space Grotesk 700 instead of Syne, to create contrast and make the product name stand out within the sentence
  • Sub-text: Space Grotesk 400, 18px desktop / 15px mobile
  • Sub-text color: rgba(253, 246, 236, 0.5)

Banner position:

  • Centered horizontally
  • Positioned at 25% from top of viewport (desktop), 20% (mobile)
  • Sits above the isometric world, not overlapping rooms
  • If viewport is short (< 700px), position at 15% from top

Banner hold: Stays visible for 2.5 seconds after full entrance, then fades upward:

  • translateY(0) to translateY(-30px), opacity 1 to 0, 400ms ease-in
  • Sub-text fades 100ms before headline

Beat 6: First Interaction Prompt (8.0s - 8.5s+)

Duration: 500ms entrance, then persistent

What happens: The chat bar invites the client to speak. This is the transition from "watching a show" to "using a product."

Chat bar animation:

  1. Border pulse (8.0s): Chat bar bottom border color animates from transparent to --onb-accent at 40% opacity, 800ms ease-in-out, 3 cycles. Subtle. Not aggressive.
  2. Placeholder typewriter (8.2s): "Say hello to your team..." types into the chat bar placeholder, 40ms per character. Uses a slightly brighter placeholder color than normal (rgba(253, 246, 236, 0.5) instead of the usual 0.3).
  3. Cursor blink: Standard text cursor blink in the input field after placeholder completes.
  4. Mini-map fade (8.0s): Mini-map component fades in at bottom-left, opacity 0 to 1, 500ms ease-in-out. Shows the current camera position.
  5. HUD fade (8.3s): The task HUD bar at the top fades in, 300ms ease-in-out. Shows "No tasks yet" in a gentle state.

After the prompt:

  • Client clicks the chat bar or types -> standard Corner chat experience begins
  • Client clicks a room -> camera pans to that room, agent's chat opens
  • The "onboarding" is complete. They're in Corner now.

The Full Timeline

Time Beat What Happens
0.0s 0 Stillness. Floor plan dims to 5%.
0.8s 1 Isometric world materializes. Walls rise, floors texture, lighting fades in, particles drift.
2.3s 2 Rooms snap in one by one (center-out). Thud ripples. Camera drifts from 0.7x to 0.8x.
4.0s 3 Agent sprites fade in at desks. Nameplates appear. Status dots go green.
5.2s 4 3-4 agents greet with speech bubbles. Typewriter text. Camera zooms 0.8x to 1.2x.
6.5s 5 "Welcome to your Corner" banner drops in. Orange underline draws.
8.0s 6 Chat bar pulses. Placeholder types. Mini-map and HUD fade in.
8.5s -- Client is in Corner. Onboarding complete.

Performance Requirements

This is a choreographed animation sequence. It must be smooth.

  • Target: 60fps throughout the entire 8.5 seconds
  • No layout thrashing: All animations use transform/opacity only (GPU-composited). No width/height/top/left animations.
  • Particle system: Canvas-based (not DOM elements). 60 particles max. Each particle is a single drawRect call.
  • Sprite loading: All agent sprites and room assets must be preloaded during the loading screen (Beat 7 of onboarding). By the time the reveal starts, every asset is in the browser cache.
  • Fallback: If any asset fails to load, skip its individual animation and move to the next beat. Never stall the sequence.
  • Low-end devices: Detect performance via navigator.hardwareConcurrency. If < 4 cores:
    • Reduce particles to 20
    • Skip thud ripples
    • Reduce stagger to 80ms (faster sequence)
    • Skip the camera zoom (stay at 1.0x)

Mobile Adaptations

Phone (390px)

  • Banner: 28px headline, 14px sub-text
  • Rooms snap in at 80ms stagger (faster to compensate for smaller viewport)
  • Agent greetings: Only 2 (not 4). Shorter text (max 30 chars)
  • Speech bubbles: Positioned to avoid overlapping on small screens
  • Camera: Starts at 0.5x (more zoomed out to fit), ends at 0.9x
  • Chat bar is already in the thumb zone -- just pulse it

Tablet (768px)

  • Banner: 36px headline, 16px sub-text
  • 3 greetings (not 4)
  • Camera: 0.6x to 1.1x
  • Otherwise same as desktop

Replay / Skip

Skip Button

A subtle "Skip" text link appears at bottom-right after 1 second:

  • Space Grotesk 400, 13px, rgba(253, 246, 236, 0.3)
  • On hover: opacity 0.6
  • On click: instantly jumps to Beat 6 (chat bar prompt). All rooms, agents, and UI elements appear immediately without animation.

No Replay

Once seen, the reveal never plays again. On return visits, the client goes straight to their Corner office (no onboarding, no reveal, no banner). The reveal is a one-time experience.

CSS Animation Definitions (Bobby Reference)

/* Spring easing for room snaps and banner */
--spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);

/* Smooth zoom easing */
--zoom-ease: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1);

/* Wall rise easing (fast start, slow end) */
--rise-ease: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);

/* Fade timing */
--fade-in: 200ms ease-in-out;
--fade-out: 150ms ease-in;

Orchestration Approach

Use a single requestAnimationFrame loop with a timeline controller. Not CSS animation delays (they're brittle and hard to synchronize). Each beat has a start time, duration, and easing function. The loop checks elapsed time and triggers/updates each beat accordingly.

// Pseudo-structure for Bobby
const timeline = [
  { beat: 0, start: 0,    duration: 800,  fn: dimFloorPlan },
  { beat: 1, start: 800,  duration: 1500, fn: materializeWorld },
  { beat: 2, start: 2300, duration: 1700, fn: snapRooms },
  { beat: 3, start: 4000, duration: 1200, fn: showAgents },
  { beat: 4, start: 5200, duration: 2000, fn: agentGreetings },
  { beat: 5, start: 6500, duration: 1500, fn: showBanner },
  { beat: 6, start: 8000, duration: 500,  fn: showChatPrompt },
];

Testing Criteria

When Bobby builds this, the reveal should:

  1. Run at 60fps on a 2020 MacBook Air (M1, base spec)
  2. Complete in exactly 8.5 seconds (tolerance: +/- 200ms)
  3. Look intentional on every frame (no visible jank, no elements popping in unexpectedly)
  4. Make someone who's never seen it go "whoa" or "that's cool"
  5. Feel like a game introduction cutscene, not a web app loading screen
  6. Work on mobile at 390px without layout breaks

This is the moment that sells the product. A plumber in Phoenix just spent 5 minutes answering questions about their business. They're skeptical. They've seen a hundred dashboards. Then their Corner appears, their agents greet them by name, and suddenly it's not software. It's their team. That's the reveal.
